title: The Weaver and the Wyrm
summary: How the two corrupted powers of the Triat feed each other.

claims.text: Because the Wyrm is caught inside the Pattern Web, it hates the Weaver's works most yet finds them easiest to corrupt.
The Weaver often misses this, or takes what happens as serving its own plan: a world frozen in perfect, unchanging order.
Almost everything has the Weaver's mark, since fixed form and substance are its work; even animals that use simple tools carry a trace of it.
A Wendigo Theurge of Newfoundland tells how the great auks were slaughtered and boiled for oil to fuel machines, men doing the Wyrm's work for the Weaver.

title: The Machine and the Digital Web
summary: The newest and fastest-growing Weaver power.

claims.text: Computers and the Internet have sharpened the Onesong, the communion of Weaver-spirits, and a single spirit in the Pattern Web can now call swarms of Pattern Spiders in seconds.
The Digital Web is weaving itself into the Pattern Web, and both webs grow tighter each year.
Pattern Spiders work to calcify the Penumbra; if they succeed, the spirit world will choke on webbing and Earth will become one endless city.
The Machine, a spirit that grew with human technology, is waking toward full awareness and may become a Celestine; Glass Walker Theurges argue whether it would help or rival Gaia.

title: Spiders of the Weaver
summary: Some of the many spider-spirits that serve the Weaver.

claims.text: Guardian-Spiders look like clumps of webbing, defend and mend the Pattern Web to the death, and never leave its side.
Mind-Spiders spread the Web into Epiphs and Dream Realms in swarms of thousands that send other spirits fleeing.
Nano-Spiders, too small to see unaided, first hatched only twenty or thirty years ago after long silence, and Weaver servants take them as a sign the Weaver may yet recover.
Leaks suggest some alliance between Pentex and a Technocracy special projects division, though far from a smooth one.
Some say Pentex sought out the tech-mages to give the Wyrm a new way into the world; mages say both are small fish beside the Syndicate, and conspiracy buffs call it all a military front.
